text: Re-scoped and MEASURED 2026-09-25: NOT a zoom-cull or camera/perf-mod bug. Root cause is vanilla body-hidden-when-swimming rendering: PawnRenderNodeWorker_Body.CanDrawNow() returns false when PawnRenderFlags.NoBody is set (set when Pawn.Swimming=CurJob.swimming); PawnRenderNodeWorker_Head never checks NoBody, so the head keeps drawing. Screenshot proof: Holmes (Human822690) at (112,12) renders as a floating head with no body above the beach line. get_cell_info confirms (112,12) terrain=RUT_ScaldMargin -- our own WaterShallowBase-derived custom terrain (TerminalBiomes/Defs/TerrainDefs/RUT_ScaldMargin.xml) -- so vanilla correctly reads him as standing in water and hides the body; this part is not a bug. Hicks vanishes on dry Sand nearby, consistent with a stale CurJob.swimming flag not clearing after leaving our water, combined with PawnRenderer's useCached path (Find.CameraDriver.ZoomRootSize>18f uses a cached humanlike atlas; <=18f always renders the live tree honoring whatever NoBody state is current) -- this explains the zoom-dependent flicker without any screen-rect culling bug. Ollopom/RM_Shulla vanishing but Dactillion/RM_Noohm not tracks the same mechanism via DrawNonHumanlikeSwimmingGraphic: only PawnKindDefs with swimmingGraphicData set get a swim sprite when Swimming; without one a submerged small animal falls into the same suppressed-body rendering. FOUNDRY 2026-09-26, offline (c2f437523). ROOT CAUSE of the flat read FOUND and it was structural, not a timid constant: RM_MapComponent_WaterAgitation fired ONE ripple per interval MAP-WIDE (~0.014 spawns/tick at its fastest). A camera sees ~3 percent of a map and FleckDef WaterRipple lives ~4.1s (fadeOutTime 4, solidTime 0, alpha 0.2 - MEASURED from the def), so the expected number of ripples visible at any moment was about one tenth of one. Re-tuning the old LightRipple/HeavyRipple constants could never have fixed it. REWRITTEN: the component now samples cells from Find.CameraDriver.CurrentViewRect, so ripple density is proportional to how much of the VIEW is agitated water and total cost is bounded by the sample count regardless of map size (<=0.5 fleck spawns/tick at 1x). Per-cell byte grid replaces the cell-list pools; skips entirely when this is not the current map. At defaults a viewful of heavy water settles near 120 concurrent ripples, about one per 16 visible cells. NEW Mod Settings slider waterAgitationDensity (0-4x, default 1x, setting 51a) because the direction was given and the figure was not. SECOND lever, zero C# and probably the bigger visual win: terrain fleckData + throwFleckChance (AirPuff, angled upward) now on all six boil terrains at 0.75 deep / 0.45 shallow and on RUT_ScaldMargin at 0.08 - the engine's own SteadyEnvironmentEffects route, which visits ceil(area*0.0006) cells per tick (MEASURED in the decompile), well above Odyssey HotSpring's own 0.25. Also corrected burnDamage to what it DOES: HediffGiver_Terrain applies Max(burnDamage,3) so the authored 1/2 were both silently 3; now 3 shallow / 4 deep per the 2026-09-25 deep-water ruling. title: shared_sync.py silently drops a peer commit made during its run: reset --keep moves HEAD past work that was never in its todo set, and origin/main..HEAD then reads clean
spec: MEASURED 2026-09-26: a 16-file commit by the Grey Sea build agent vanished from HEAD during a peer's shared_sync.py run; git log origin/main..HEAD printed nothing, which reads as 'all pushed'. Recovered byte-exact from the dropped commit's blobs. MECHANISM, read off src/RimMandrake/Utils/shared_sync.py: todo is computed at ~line 78 (git rev-list --cherry-pick --right-only UP...HEAD), the replay+push publishes exactly that set, then ~line 123 runs git reset --keep UP. One tree, one HEAD, four agents => any commit that lands on HEAD between those two points is never in todo, is never pushed, and reset --keep moves HEAD past it. No warning; survives only in the reflog. FIX: re-read HEAD immediately before the reset and compare it to the HEAD todo was computed from; if it moved, abort (or loop) rather than reset. Until fixed, every caller must prove survival with git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main. Recorded in CLAUDE.md's Git section.

title: One gravship can only ever visit ONE sea floor: MapPortal caches its pocket map, so the hatch's per-tile biome resolution runs once and every later dive re-enters the first sea
spec: MEASURED 2026-09-26 from the decompiled engine (RimSage, RimWorld/MapPortal.cs lines 12-340) plus our own source. DEFECT: RM_SeaDiveHatch (src/RimMandrake/DivingInteraction/Source/RM_SeaDiveHatch.cs) overrides ONLY GeneratePocketMapInt(). In vanilla MapPortal, GetOtherMap() reads 'if (PocketMap == null) GeneratePocketMap();' and GeneratePocketMap() is the ONLY caller of GeneratePocketMapInt(). The field 'protected Map pocketMap' is Scribed (Scribe_References.Look(ref pocketMap, "pocketMap")) and is nulled only when map.Parent?.HasMap == false. => The pocket map is generated ONCE per hatch and reused forever. CONSEQUENCE: the hatch is a building on the gravship and travels with it. Dive at the Twilight Sea -> ResolveGeneratorForCurrentTile() picks RM_SeaDiveGenerator_TwilightSea, generates, caches. Fly to the Grey Sea and dive -> PocketMap is non-null, so GeneratePocketMapInt() is never called again and the party re-enters the TWILIGHT floor. Three of the four seas are unreachable to a given ship after its first dive. The per-tile resolution in ResolveGeneratorForCurrentTile() is careful and correct and is DEAD CODE after the first dive, which is why the class reads as right. Note the vanilla 'view pocket map' gizmo also hardcodes def.portal.pocketMapGenerator.label, so a Twilight hatch will mislabel too. FIX SHAPE (not ruled): either key a map per sea on the hatch (a Dictionary<string biomeDefName, Map>, all Scribed) and override GetOtherMap() to select by the parent map's current biome, or release/regenerate when the current tile's sea differs from the cached map's. Persistence-vs-regenerate is owner question 8 of design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_twilight_deep_bedazzle_2026-09-26.md - a persisted floor per sea is the richer answer and is what players will expect after building a base down there. Surfaced by the Twilight bedazzle design pass; BENCH verified it against the engine before filing.

text: SUPERSEDED IN APPROACH, 2026-09-26, and the immediate bleeding is stopped. (1) A SECOND defect was found under this one: PocketMapProperties.destroyOnParentMapAbandoned defaults to TRUE and none of our four generators set it, so Game.cs destroys every pocket map whose sourceMap is an abandoned map and GravshipUtility.AbandonMap fires on takeoff from an unanchored tile - the sea floor was already being destroyed AT TAKEOFF, before the ship landed. The bug cannot be expressed in that architecture. Owner's keep-or-discard requirement becomes WorldObjectCompProperties_Abandon on a real world object, one line. (3) Reference implementation found: the installed mod GravTide (gravtide.mod, workshop 3779600989) already does exactly this and ships full C# source; we harvest technique and take no dependency. text: TWILIGHT SITTING 2026-09-26, two further owner directions. RECORDED WITHOUT THE QUOTE FLAG: he said both in-session, but they arrived as mid-turn relayed messages and block_forged_owner_said.py cannot see those, so --owner-said is refused. Substance is his; the exact-words provenance is not claimed. (A) THE GROWN LIGHTS ARE CHAINABLE TOO. The glowing plant should also be chainable so the player moves them around constantly to optimise; his stated reason was player appetite for exactly that fidget. => Both halves of the light economy are mobile: the waveglass's skylight drifts on its own over about a week, the floating field cages are chained and walkable, and the cultivated lights (noothelm/hoolimbre/sun-sphere line) are chained and movable too. Intended play is a constantly re-arranged floating constellation of fields and lamps. CONSEQUENCES: a grown light that MOVES cannot be a stationary CompGlower building - same root problem as the already-filed 'glowers do not follow a moving pawn' gap, and both should be solved by ONE mechanism. It also gives the tethered cage a second reason to exist beyond vertical space: a cage is what you clip a crop AND a lamp to. OPEN BALANCE QUESTION, not yet put to him: is moving a lamp cheap and constant (a haul job) or deliberate and costly (a rebuild)? 'Constantly' argues cheap, but cheap times many lamps is a micromanagement tax rather than a pleasure. (B) THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS NOW COMMISSIONED: he asked for the really cool things on the ground that you CANNOT move, that are therefore harder to maintain, and that are worth it anyway. => The biome needs a third class beside the mobile fields and mobile lamps: fixed, high-value, maintenance-hungry installations that justify staying put in an ocean where the light walks away. Design pass owed.

TWILIGHT SITTING 2026-09-26/27, three more rulings, all DECISIONS TAKEN BY QUESTION CARD (our wording, clicked - not owner quotes, no --owner-said). (1) THE IMMOBILE PRIZE IS THE BANK WORKS. Of four candidates (held-open skylight, canopy station, ghallowyn hall, bank works) he picked the bank works: the dry rivers are fixed geography, their banks are the richest ground on the floor, the stake-line must be held against the current, and one breach takes the whole thing downstream. 🔑 NOTE THE COUPLING THIS CREATES: he had already ruled the rivers STILL CARRY A PAWN (ban 3 live, owes new C#). The river is now load-bearing twice - it is the hazard AND the site of the biome's anchor prize. The richest ground is deliberately next to the thing that will kill you, and the stake-line is both the farm boundary and the safety tell (thessmoss already stops dead at it, per the content pass). ⇒ The river current mechanism is no longer optional or deferrable: the immobile prize depends on it. Scope them as ONE piece of work, not two. The other three candidates are NOT rejected, only not chosen as the anchor - keep them on the shelf. (2) MOVE COST: CHEAP HAUL, MINUTES. A colonist unclips a lamp or a cage and walks it over. Constant repositioning is the intended pleasure. ⚠️ ACCEPTED RISK, stated on the card: cheap times many lamps becomes a micromanagement tax, so the LAMP COUNT MUST STAY SMALL - a handful, not twenty. That is a balance constraint on the design, not a detail; whoever tunes it must cap the useful number of lamps rather than let the player carpet the floor. (3) THE WAVEGLASS RENAME GOES NOW, AS ONE PASS, INCLUDING RM_MoldMatRoof - the ceiling organism another agent shipped under the old name hours after the ruling. ~11 shipped descriptions plus that def.

TWILIGHT SITTING 2026-09-27, owner rulings + A CORRECTION BENCH OWES. (0) 🔴 CORRECTION, BENCH WAS WRONG: I told the owner we could not use ordinary Plant defs on a sea floor and had to use a custom sessile ThingWithComps. He challenged it ('I've seen plants on other planet layers'). He is right. MEASURED from the decompiled engine: MapPlantGrowthRateCalculator.BuildFor(Map) does tile=map.Tile; LongLatOf(map.Tile); OutdoorTemperatureAt(tile,...). That throws on a POCKET map, whose Tile is invalid - it is a pocket-map trap, NOT a planet-layer one. A seabed LAYER tile is a real registered tile with a real id and lat/long, so ordinary plants work normally there. GravTide's custom SessileLife class was a DESIGN choice (avoiding plant-slot exclusion and pawn-AI overhead for 28 coral taxa), never an engine prohibition, and I relayed it as if it were. ⇒ On the seabed layer we may use plain Plant defs. A custom class is optional, chosen per-need. ⚠️ One real subtlety to carry forward: the calculator uses GenCelestial.CelestialSunGlow(tile,...) for light, so cached growth rates assume surface sunlight - a depth-darkening GameCondition will not be reflected in them. Flagged, not solved. (1) THE CEILING IS NOT A FLOOR PLANT. RM_MoldMatRoof shipped as a full <plant> def (growDays 26, harvestWork 240, recoloured Echeveria texture) growing on the floor. Owner: it should NOT be a plant or sessile on the floor - instead A BIG PANEL THAT OCCASIONALLY FLOATS DOWN AND CAN BE HARVESTED. An event plus an item, not vegetation. RM_MoldMatRoof is RETIRED AND REDESIGNED, not renamed; the waveglass rename pass was told to skip it and leave its wildPlants row alone. (2) THE HELD-OPEN SKYLIGHT IS OUT. Owner: 'I'm actually not excited by the players cutting open a hole. it's way too far above you.' The ceiling is a SKY, not a surface a pawn can work. Nothing may imply reaching it. (3) THE BEAMS: coloured shafts shining to the floor, shifting slowly, VARYING IN COLOUR, with darkness between them - plus the shadows of the great whale analogues AND of fish. (4) 🔴 OWNER-FLAGGED GAP: 'we haven't detailed almost anything dangerous down here! That's a problem.' The Twilight currently has ONE predator (RM_Loohn) and the river current. The Grey has brine-pool encasement; the Scald has boiling water, steam and an exposure clock. The Twilight is the safe sea, and that makes it dull. DANGER DESIGN IS NOW THE LIVE WORK.
